test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A dealer marks his goods at 57% above the cost price and allows a discount of 22% on the marked price. What is his gain percentage (correct to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net effect formula: (1 + markup) × (1 − discount)

= 1.57 × 0.78

= 1.2246

Gain % = (1.2246 − 1) × 100 = 22.46%

**∴ Answer = 22.46% gain**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price is 57% above cost price

Discount = 22%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − Discount)

Gain % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ Marked Price = 100 + 57 = 157

⇒ Discount = 22% of 157 = 34.54

⇒ Selling Price = 157 − 34.54 = 122.46

⇒ Gain = 122.46 − 100 = 22.46

⇒ Gain % = 22.46%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.46% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

Net effect = a + b + (a×b)/100 when two percentage changes are applied.

Marked Price Concept

Marked price is the listed price before discount.

Discount Formula

Discount = MP − SP

Profit Formula

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100
